(3) FY28 FCF of ~$16.7/share at a 3.4% yield plus $8 net cash = $499. Weighted 45/35/20 this gives ~$505, roughly spot.

FY27 is cross-checked by Yahoo ($18.48, 34 analysts). [citation gate 2026-10-15: the figures are on the MarketScreener AMAT finances page (source 15, URL corrected to id 4850): FY28 EPS 23.85, FY27 EPS 18.43, net sales 46,312M (FY27) and 55,857M (FY28) on 2026-10-15, i.e. +0.3%/+0.6% revenue drift since 2026-09-29. Yahoo (source 5) covers FY27 only ($18.47, 35 analysts, range $16.02-21.77 on 2026-10-15) and has no FY28 estimates.]

At Sep-2027 the NTM period is almost entirely FY28. I take ~6% off the $23.85 consensus because two-year-forward semi-cap estimates are usually cut when the cycle turns (Nomad Semi cycle history). SEMI's July (+21.8% 2027, +14.1% 2028 WFE) and September ($220B 2028 WFE) forecasts argue against a larger haircut.

GuruFocus showed a forward P/E of 25.92 on 2026-09-27 (source 9; aggregator, EPS basis not stated); on this run's consensus the stock is at $512.01 / $18.43 = 27.8x FY27 (citation gate 2026-10-15). AMAT's 5-10 year average trailing P/E is ~18-22x, and quoted 5-year forward averages run to ~24-25x. On earnings two years into an upcycle, I apply a multiple in the lower half of that forward range (22x) rather than holding today's ~26-28x.

Cash plus investments $14.50B, less debt $6.54B, = $7.96B ($10.0/share on 793.6M shares). I partly discount the $2.42B of strategic equity stakes, which gives ~$8/share. This follows the supervisor's 10-Q reconciliation. [citation gate 2026-10-15: estimate, not a reported figure. The 10-Q (July 26, 2026) gives net cash $7,957M = cash 7,037 + short-term investments 2,196 + long-term investments 5,268 less short-term debt 1,299 and long-term debt 5,245, i.e. $10.03/share on 793.6M shares outstanding, or $6.98/share excluding the $2,421M of equity investments; counting half the stakes gives $8.50. ~$8 is a judgment inside that range; see citation_audit.json agent_leg_issues.]

800M diluted in FQ3; buybacks slowed to $400M/quarter ($1.14B over 9M), so only modest shrinkage by Sep-2027.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established that my decisive growth input was stale. I used SEMI's Dec-2025 forecast (+7-8% equipment growth in 2027), but the July 14 2026 mid-year release has WFE +23.1% in 2026, +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028 to ~$200B. I verified this, and found SEMI raised 2028 WFE further to ~$220B at SEMICON Taiwan (Digitimes, 2026-09-01). My +8% FY28 growth assumption therefore goes. I now anchor on FY28 consensus EPS of $23.85, with a smaller ~6% late-cycle haircut to $22.5. I also dropped the Polymarket recession figure as a valuation driver, since it came from a blocked snippet and is macro context only. I replaced the mixed-basis 19x trailing median with a 21-22x forward multiple, which sits between the trailing average and the ~25x forward 5-year average quoted by data vendors. I also dropped the FY27 x 25x leg, because at Sep-2027 the market values FY28. Net cash is now $8/share. Fair value rises from $455 to ~$505, close to spot. Base rates still drive the shape. AMAT has 60% realized vol, fell 29% from its $723 closing high to a $415 low within three months, and semi-cap has drawn down ~30% in 2018 and ~50% in 2022; all of this justifies a fat left tail. The distribution is lognormal with median ~$520 (fair value ~$505 plus a modest nod to still-rising WFE and upward revisions) and sigma ~0.50, with the left tail thickened slightly for the Jan-2027 Affiliates Rule deadline and cycle-turn risk. That gives P(>=512) = 0.515, vs 0.49 in round 1. Scenarios are $310/$530/$810 at 25/50/25. Research was limited to ~9 queries, and GuruFocus and MarketScreener fetches failed or returned the wrong page, so the FY28 consensus relies on the supervisor's MarketScreener read. No option data was used.

supervisor.confidence_reason: The round-2 forecasters converged on the round-1 fact-checks, so the mean already carries them. My one new fact is SEMI's Sept 1 upgrade of 2028 WFE to $220B (a named SEMI director, reported by Digitimes). It undercuts the specific reason three agents gave for 8-10% EPS haircuts, which justifies a small ~1.5% upward shift. But consensus likely already reflects it, and the Sept-2027 multiple, which no search can settle, dominates. The agents' convergence is also partly herding on one supervisor's inputs.
